_purpose: Claude's drafted listening-preferences sections, parked here after the concurrent-edit collision. Merge into music.json below 'Original Works' if wanted, or delete.

items.name: Caroline Shaw
items.note: The Partita's Sarabande is a masterpiece outright; Reich's descendant with a voice-first imagination.

items.name: Donnacha Dennehy
items.note: Just-intonation spectralism tuned to a sean-nós voice — sounds simultaneously ancient and unwritten.

items.name: Kaija Saariaho
items.note: Spectral timbre with genuine dramatic depth; each period a different instrument.

items.name: Philip Glass
items.note: The Akhnaten / Koyaanisqatsi side — process music at liturgical scale.

items.name: Steve Reich
items.note: Pulse and phase as architecture; the more load-bearing minimalist for the current scene.

items.name: Sarah Goldfeather
items.note: Mouth Full of Ears started a whole hunt — theatrical extended technique that actually lands.

items.title: Partita for 8 Voices
items.note: Start at the Sarabande; the Passacaglia is the summit.

items.title: Grá agus Bás
items.note: Drone plus lament — the oldest formal substrate there is, retuned.

items.title: Music for 18 Musicians
items.note: The pulse the whole post-minimal world still writes against.

items.title: Mouth Full of Ears
items.note: Unconventional sound with clear dramatic direction — the reference point.

items.name: Contemporary classical / new music
items.note: The Bang on a Can lineage and after; drama over dogma.

items.name: Spectralism
items.note: Timbre as harmony, harmony as physics — Grisey through Saariaho and into the present.

items.name: Minimalism and after
items.note: Reich more than Glass, and everyone downstream of both.

items.name: The ancient–modern seam
items.note: Sean-nós, drone, lament — where medieval and new music turn out to be the same music.
